title: Evaluation of Antimicrobial Activities of Nanoparticles and Nanostructured Surfaces In Vitro
protocol: Sterilize MgO nanoparticles in a 200 °C convection oven for 60 min prior to each in vitro experiment.
Disinfect all samples using UV radiation for 2 hours before initiation of in vitro studies.
Alternatively, use ethylene oxide (EtO) for sterilization of heat-sensitive materials.
Retrieve bacteria cell stocks from storage at -80 °C.
Add 10 µL of each bacteria cell stock into 5 mL of an appropriate growth medium.
Place the inoculated medium into an incubator-shaker at 37 °C and 250 rpm for approximately 16 hours overnight.
Subculture Staphylococcus species by placing 400 µL of each overnight culture into 20 mL of fresh growth medium (ratio of 100 µL/5 mL).
Incubate the cultures with shaking at 37 °C and 250 rpm for an additional 4-6 hours.
Collect bacteria from the overnight cultures by aliquoting 1 mL into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the collected bacteria at 1,956 × g for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and place it into a collection receptacle.
Resuspend the cell pellets in 0.5 mL of fresh growth medium.
Combine two 0.5 mL suspensions to create 1 mL of suspension.
Repeat the centrifugation process at 1,956 × g for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellets in fresh growth medium.
Repeat the second wash cycle using fresh growth medium as described earlier.
Resuspend cell pellets in 0.33 mL of Tris buffer (pH 8.5).
Combine three suspensions, each of 0.33 mL volume, into one 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 1,956 × g.
Remove the supernatant from the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of fresh Tris buffer to create a seeding culture.
Determine the concentration of the cell suspension using a hemocytometer.
Calculate the volume of the cell suspension needed for a seeding culture of 7.8 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add the calculated volume of the cell suspension to the required volume of growth media to create the seeding bacteria culture.
Determine the actual bacteria seeding density in CFU/mL.
Create a tenfold serial dilution to 10-4.
Spread-plate the 10-4 dilution onto the appropriate growth agar.
Incubate the spread plates overnight.
Count the number of colonies after incubation.
Calculate the CFU/mL from the counted colonies.
Aliquot 2 mL of the bacterial seeding culture into each well of a 12-well plate.
Add 3 mL of bacterial seeding culture to each 5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing pre-weighed nMgO.
Vortex briefly to mix the nMgO with bacteria.
Pipette the bacteria/nMgO mixture 2-3 times before aliquoting.
Aliquot 1 mL of the mixture into three separate wells for triplicate samples.
Prepare control samples consisting of cells only, media only, and lowest/highest concentrations of nanoparticles in triplicates.
Incubate all 12-well plates at 37 °C and 120 rpm for 24 hours.
Collect every 3 mL sample from bacterial cultures by pipetting into an individual 15 mL conical tube.
Create 1:10 serial dilutions using a 96-well plate.
Add 180 µL of Tris buffer to each well in row B to row G for the appropriate number of columns.
Vortex each 15 mL conical tube containing bacterial samples briefly.
Transfer 50 µL from each vortexed sample into an individual well in row A of the 96-well plate.
Transfer 20 µL from each well in row A to an individual well in row B, mix by pipetting.
Transfer 20 µL from each well in row B to an individual well in row C, and continue this pattern until the well in row G contains 200 µL.
Pipette 100 µL of each dilution onto an appropriate growth agar plate.
Spread across the plate to disperse the cell culture.
Place the plates into an incubator-shaker overnight at 37 °C.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 24 h.
Examine the plates and count those that have approximately 25-300 colonies.
Use the number of colonies per plate to calculate the CFU/mL.
Pre-calibrate a pH meter using standardizing solutions of pH 4, pH 7, and pH 10.
Read each bacterial sample by placing the pH probe into the 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge each 15 mL conical tube for 5 min at 5,724 × g to pellet the cellular and nanoparticle debris.
Dilute 30 µL of the supernatant into 2.97 mL of 18.2 Ω filtered water to create a 1:100 dilution.
Read the samples using ICP-OES.
Prepare the desired concentrations of nanoparticles using the methods described in step 2.1-2.1.2.2.
Prepare two sets of each weight of nanoparticles to be used.
Add one set to 3 mL aliquots of bacteria culture in the logarithmic growth phase.
Add the other set to 3 mL aliquots of growth medium without bacteria as control groups.
Determine bacteriostatic and bactericidal antibiotics for the bacteria species.
Calculate the total volume of bacterial culture required for triplicate 3 mL samples for all nanoparticle, antibiotic, and control samples.
Adjust the total volume needed if spectrophotometry is planned to accommodate cuvette volumes of 0.5 mL to 1.0 mL.
Create overnight stocks for each in vitro experiment following step 2.2.1-2.2.2 on Day 1.
Confirm plate reader settings can accommodate a 96-well plate with an optical density of 600 nm on Day 2.
Measure samples in 200 µL aliquots using a 96-well plate.
Determine the initial bacterial culture OD600 at 0.01 for the beginning of the incubation period before adding nanoparticles and antibiotics.
Collect overnight bacteria cultures from the incubator-shaker.
Create separate bacterial cultures at an OD600 of 0.01 for each material to be tested using a container large enough to accommodate the volume of cell culture needed.
Dilute overnight bacterial samples with growth medium by placing three 200 µL aliquots of the growth medium into three wells.
Place three 200 µL aliquots of the bacterial culture into additional wells (e.g., A1 through A6).
Scan the 96-well plate using a plate reader.
Average the mean value for each well containing a triplicate sample to calculate bacterial density in suspension.
Subtract the broth sample average from the bacterial average to determine optical density of bacteria.
Continue to add broth or overnight bacterial culture as needed and repeat scanning until an OD600 of approximately 0.01 is reached.
Incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 150 rpm until logarithmic growth is reached.
Remove bacterial cultures from the incubator shaker.
Aliquot 3 mL of the OD600 0.01 bacterial culture into labeled 15 mL conical tubes for test and control samples in triplicate.
Aliquot 200 µL of the bacterial culture into three wells of a 96-well plate.
Measure the samples using the plate reader.
Calculate readings as described previously to obtain the "-0.5 h reading".
Aliquot 3 mL of sterile growth medium into labeled 15 mL conical tubes for control samples (in triplicate).
Remove 1 mL of bacterial culture or medium from each triplicate set of 15 mL conical tubes.
Place the 1 mL aliquots into a 5 mL centrifuge tube containing pre-measured nanoparticles, and vortex briefly to mix.
Return 1 mL aliquots of the bacteria/nanoparticle or medium/nanoparticle suspensions to the 15 mL conical tube to distribute the nanoparticles homogeneously.
Pipette the bacteria/nanoparticle mixture 2-3 times before each 1 mL aliquot is pipetted to maintain the nanoparticles in suspension.
Aliquot 3 mL of the incubated bacterial culture into correspondingly labeled 15 mL conical tubes.
Place the plate(s) containing samples into a plate reader and initiate scanning for the "0 h" reading.
Record all data as described previously in step 3.4.2.2 and step 3.4.2.6.
Repeat the steps described to obtain the "0.5 h" reading approximately 15 min after completing the 0 h reading.
Retrieve overnight bacterial culture from the incubator-shaker.
Wash and collect bacteria, replacing fresh medium with revised simulated body fluid (rSBF) for each washing step.
Remove the supernatant from the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of rSBF supplemented with 10% FBS.
Determine the cell suspension concentration using a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cell suspension to a concentration of 7.5 × 10^5 cells/mL in rSBF supplemented with 10% FBS.
Create a seeding culture following step 2.4.1.
Determine the actual seeding density following step 2.4.2.
Distribute bacterial cell suspension onto the samples in the culture wells.
Place both the samples and control samples into individual wells of a 48-well, non-tissue treated polystyrene plate.
Aliquot 0.75 mL of the cell suspension into each well containing the samples and controls.
Place the 48-well plate(s) into an incubator-shaker for 24 h at 37 °C with shaking at 120 rpm.
Collect the samples after 24 h of incubation.
Place the collected samples into separate, labeled collection tubes.
Collect two samples from each group and place them into labeled 5.0 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 2 mL of rSBF to each tube.
Place the samples in a sonication bath and sonicate for 10 min.
Vortex each sample for 5 s after each 5 min period.
Collect the rSBF containing detached bacterial cells and place into labeled, fresh microcentrifuge tubes.
Serially dilute and plate the bacterial suspension following step 2.6.2-2.6.6.
Evaluate the post-incubation pH of culture media by following step 2.7.
Prepare the post-culture medium for ICP-OES by following methods described in step 2.8.
Create a bacterial seeding culture following procedures in step 2.2.1-2.2.2.1.
Confirm the actual seeding density following step 2.4.2.
Prepare the samples to a size of 1 × 1 cm² in a square shape.
Prepare all sample types in triplicate.
Place the samples on a three-dimensional holder if necessary.
Position the sample and holder into a well of a non-tissue culture-treated polystyrene well plate.
Trim sterilized nitrocellulose papers to a diameter of 1 cm.
Place the prepared nitrocellulose papers onto an agar plate with appropriate medium.
Pipette 50 µL of diluted bacterial culture onto the filter paper.
Pipette 50 µL of appropriate medium onto the center of each sample surface.
Pick up the nitrocellulose paper from the surface of the agar using sterilized tweezers.
Flip the nitrocellulose paper and place it onto the sample surface to contact bacteria with the medium.
Add 1 mL of Tris buffer to each well containing a sample to maintain humidity.
Incubate the polystyrene well plate at 37 °C for 24 h.
Collect the nitrocellulose paper from each sample surface.
Place each collected filter into 5 mL of Tris buffer.
Vortex the collected filter papers and nanosurfaced material samples for 5 s.
Sonicate each sample for 10 min.
Vortex the samples again after 5 min and once more after 10 min.
Collect the Tris buffer suspensions from all samples.
Place each volume into individual fresh collection tubes.
Serially dilute and plate the samples following steps 2.6.2-2.6.6.
After overnight incubation, add 10% glutaraldehyde into each well of a 48-well non-tissue treated polystyrene plate until fully covered.
Incubate the samples for 1 hour to fix bacterial cells.
Aspirate the glutaraldehyde and rinse all samples three times with Tris buffer solution to remove non-adherent bacteria.
Dehydrate the samples using 30%, 75%, and 100% ethanol, each for 30 minutes.
Use a critical point dryer to dry the samples; avoid air-drying at room temperature.
Fix samples onto an SEM stub using conductive adhesive tapes such as copper or carbon tapes.
Coat sample surfaces via sputter coating to provide conductivity before imaging, e.g., coat Mg plates with adhered bacteria under platinum/palladium (Pt/Pd) for 45 seconds at 20 mA.

Take images of the bacteria on the samples using SEM with an appropriate working distance and accelerating voltage, such as a secondary electron detector at a working distance of 5 mm and an accelerating voltage of 10 kV.
Examine surface morphology of post-culture nanomaterial samples using SEM.
Wash the samples using Tris buffer 3 times to remove free bacteria not attached to the sample.
Disperse nanoparticles into a solvent that does not affect the sample properties through ultrasonication for better dispersion when needed.
Dry the washed samples after the washing procedure.
Adhere the samples onto the SEM stub using carbon or copper double-sided adhesive tapes.
Create a conductive surface layer of Pt/Pd using a sputter coater before imaging.
Take the sample images as described in step 6.1.5.
Analyze the surface elemental composition using EDS with an appropriate accelerating voltage and desired magnifications, e.g., at 10 kV after SEM analysis.
Prepare samples for fluorescence microscopy by washing them with Tris buffer 3 times.
Air-dry the washed samples at room temperature.
Stain each sample with 10 μM thioflavin T fluorescence dye following an established protocol.
Perform fluorescence imaging of bacterial adhesion using an inverted microscope coupled with an electron-multiplying charge-coupled device digital camera.
